policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'he sought no more again for him' renders the verb of adding/repeating identically whether it is the qere perfect yasaph or the ketiv imperfect yosiph; no wording, supply, or mapped note distinguishes them. Base qere fallback carries the projection.

ASV text reads 'the Girzites', the consonant order g-r-z of the ketiv והגרזי; the textual_variant note 'Another reading is, Gizrites' gives the qere וְהַגִּזְרִי (g-z-r) as the reading not taken. The ASV rendered the ketiv.
